draft.title: A personal and informed reading
card: A personal and informed reading is your own argument about a text. It rests on solid grounds. It is not a guess, and it is not a summary of what others have said.
Close evidence
specific details from the text, such as word choices, images or structure, with analysis of how they shape meaning.
Awareness
knowing the text's context and that other readers may read it differently. This lets you place your view among them.
Judgement
your own decision about what the text achieves and how well it does so. You state it and defend it with the evidence.
draft.remember: Your own view, backed by close evidence and an awareness of context and other readings.

a.q: Which sentence from a Year 12 response best shows a personal and informed reading?
opts: The cold imagery builds a bleak mood, and I argue this is the novel's strongest choice
I just feel the novel is very sad, and I enjoyed it a great deal
The novel is about a family who move to a new town and struggle
Critics say the novel is about loss, so I accept that it is
a.why: The first sentence names specific evidence, makes a claim about meaning and judges what the writer achieves. The last option relies only on other readers and offers no judgement of the student's own, so it is not a personal reading.
a.clue: Look for evidence plus the student's own judgement.

b.q: Kai writes that a poem's broken line breaks show grief, and quotes the lines. He explains how they affect a reader and notes that others read the poem as hopeful. What is the main thing missing from his paragraph?
opts: His own judgement about what the poem achieves
Close evidence from the poem itself
Any awareness that other readings exist
A summary of the poem's events
b.why: Kai has close evidence, with quotes and analysis, and he shows awareness of another reading. He does not say what the poem achieves overall or argue why his view holds. A summary is not what makes a reading informed, so it is not the gap.
b.clue: Check which of the three parts he has not shown.

proposal.title: A personal and informed reading
card: A personal and informed reading is your own argument about a text. It rests on solid grounds. It is not a guess, and it is not a summary of what others have said.
Close evidence
specific details from the text, such as word choices, images or structure, with analysis of how they shape meaning.
Awareness
knowing the text's context and that other readers may read it differently. This lets you place your view among theirs.
Judgement
your own evaluation of what the text achieves and how well it does so. Explaining what a detail means is analysis. Saying whether it works is judgement.
proposal.remember: Evidence and awareness support your own verdict on what the text achieves and how well.

a.q: Which sentence from a Year 12 response best shows a personal and informed reading?
opts: Cold imagery builds a bleak mood, the novel's best choice
I feel the novel is very sad, and I enjoyed it a lot
The novel follows a family who move town and struggle
Critics say the novel is about loss, so I accept that
a.why: The first sentence points to specific evidence, says how it shapes meaning and judges how well it works. The critics option leans only on other readers and offers no judgement of the student's own, so it is not a personal reading.
a.clue: Look for evidence plus the student's own verdict.

b.q: Kai quotes a poem's broken line breaks and analyses how they suggest grief. He links this to the poet's recent loss of a parent and notes that some readers find the poem hopeful. Which part is missing?
opts: A judgement of how well the poem achieves its effect
Close evidence with analysis of the lines
Awareness of the poem's context
Awareness that other readings exist
b.why: Kai quotes and analyses the lines, places them in the poet's context and notes a different reading. He explains what the line breaks mean, but never evaluates how well the poem achieves its effect. Close evidence is tempting, but quoting and analysing the lines is exactly that.
b.clue: Explaining meaning is not the same as judging success.
